# finport-optengine

> A multi-asset portfolio optimization engine that reports the evidence
> behind an allocation, not just the weights. Every solve returns which
> solver answered, whether the constraints actually held, how
> well-conditioned the covariance estimate was, how concentrated the book is
> in risk rather than capital, how much of the backtest survives out of
> sample, and how much of that survives the number of configurations tried
> before settling on one.

Install `finport-optengine`, import `optimization_engine`, run `optengine`.
The three names differ because the obvious distribution name was taken on
PyPI. Python 3.9+. MIT.

The core install is numpy, pandas, scipy, cvxpy, scs and scikit-learn.
Plotting (`viz`), Excel I/O (`excel`), regression-based benchmark metrics
(`stats`), the MCP server (`mcp`, Python 3.10+), the Streamlit app (`ui`) and
network data providers (`data`) are extras; `all` covers everything but the
app and the server. Reaching a feature whose extra is missing raises with the
install command that fixes it.

Three ways in. As a library, importing `optimization_engine`. As a CLI,
`optengine`, where `optimize`, `backtest`, `check` and `describe` take
`--json` and put one parseable document on stdout. As an MCP server,
`pip install "finport-optengine[mcp]"` then `optengine-mcp`, which speaks
stdio and exposes five tools — `list_optimizers`, `describe_optimizer`,
`check_mandate`, `optimize`, `backtest` — returning those same payloads.

Twelve optimizers (mean-variance, max-Sharpe, min-variance, risk parity,
HRP, HERC, NCO, CVaR, CDaR, Black-Litterman, max-diversification, equal
weight and inverse volatility), seven covariance estimators with
Marchenko-Pastur denoising, a stateless backtest core with a square-root
market-impact cost model, walk-forward and final-holdout paths, and
selection-bias diagnostics (deflated Sharpe, probability of backtest
overfitting, minimum track record length).

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/AGENTS.md): API map, the `--json` CLI contract, and the mistakes that cost real debugging time — start here
- [README](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/README.md): the five questions the engine answers, with figures
- [ERRORS.md](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/docs/ERRORS.md): every exception the library raises on purpose, which to catch, the CLI's exit codes, and what is reported rather than raised
- [RESEARCH.md](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH.md): the literature behind each method, and what was deliberately left out
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed, and what to do about it

## Optional

- [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md): Trusted Publishing setup and the release procedure
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/finport-optengine/): released versions
- [Example config](https://github.com/alanvaa06/finport-optengine/blob/main/config/example_multi_asset.yaml): a working multi-asset mandate
- API reference: generated from the docstrings by `scripts/build_api_docs.py` and published to GitHub Pages from `main`. Every exported name with its signature, parameters, units and errors.
